limitations: Historical synthetic/model calibration only; no new scientific adjudication or nature-level inference.

original_claim.claim: At the R1 baseline sample size and cap, the predeclared primary bias statistic B_i detects an injected acceleration-dependent v-tilde offset of amplitude 0.05 or 0.10 (restricted to the two lowest g_N bins) with power >= 80% across the seed ladder, establishing the protocol's minimum-detectable-effect floor at or below the literature-contested anomaly scale.
original_claim.kill: Power below 80% at injected amplitude 0.10 (the larger arm) — the protocol's decision rule cannot reliably detect an effect at the scale of the literature disagreement, so a clean R1 null would not be informative.
original_claim.evidence: ORB-11222's cataloged frozen run at Orrery 28dd5c72 detects both 0.05 and 0.10 injections in 33.3% of seeds, below the 80% rule. The result makes a null uninformative; ORB-11241 owns diagnosis.

diagnostic_control.evidence: The apparatus recovers the injection cleanly. Differencing each injected seed against the same seed of the zero-injection arm gives 85% of the 0.05 amplitude and 83% of the 0.10 amplitude, positive in every seed of every arm. The frozen gate instead tested unpaired |B_i| against zero using a spread that carries the whole comparator-sampling budget, and its >=80% requirement is unreachable below 3/3 with the three seeds the frozen matrix allots.
diagnostic_control.locus: decision layer (Orrery fixture) and the frozen rule's own arithmetic
diagnostic_control.protocol_note: the 80%-of-3-seeds inconsistency is recorded, not repaired; it sits with the protocol's 47-vs-44 realization count
